STAP B:Missing values verwijderen
--- 
Sample_data
```{r}
#Aantal missing values
colSums(is.na(sample_data))

#filter stalen met te veel NA's in de metadata
data_clean <- sample_data[rowSums(is.na(sample_data)) <= 11, ]
data_clean
colSums(is.na(data_clean))

#filter metadata-kolommen die meer dan 79% ontbrekende waarden vertonen
data_clean <- data_clean[, colMeans(is.na(data_clean)) <= 0.79] 
#verwijderen niet-informatieve kolommen
data_clean <- data_clean %>%
  select(-subject.race,-subject.ethnicity,-olink_batch_id)
``` 
Proteins_anno

---
STAP C: controle op dubbele eiwitten en ouliers -> misschien moeten we deze wel nog aanpassen als we wel met protein_clean werken
---

```{r}
#1.Controle op dubbele eiwitnamen
names(protein_raw)[duplicated(names(protein_raw))] 

#2.Enkel numerieke NPX-kolommen behouden
protein_raw_numeric <- protein_raw[, -1]

#3. Outlierdetectie per eiwit
outliers <- lapply(protein_raw_numeric, function(x) {
  Q1 <- quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
  Q3 <- quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  IQR <- Q3 - Q1

  which(x < (Q1 - 1.5 * IQR) |
        x > (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR))
})

#4.Beschrijven statistieken per eiwit
protein_stats <- data.frame(
  protein = colnames(npx_only),
  min = apply(npx_only, 2, min, na.rm = TRUE),
  max = apply(npx_only, 2, max, na.rm = TRUE),
  mean = apply(npx_only, 2, mean, na.rm = TRUE),
  sd = apply(npx_only, 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE)
)

head(protein_stats)

#all_values <- unlist(protein_raw_numeric[,-1])
#boxplot(all_values,
#        horizontal =TRUE,
 #       main = "Distribution of NPX values")
```

STAP D: Is er transformatie nodig?
---

```{r}
#1.Histogrammen
set.seed(123)

selected <- sample(colnames(protein_raw)[-1], 20)

plot_data <- protein_raw %>%
  select(all_of(selected)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "Protein",
    values_to = "NPX"
  )

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = NPX)) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 30,
    fill = "steelblue",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Protein, ncol = 5) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of 20 randomly selected proteins",
    x = "NPX value",
    y = "Count"
  )

#2. QQ-plots
set.seed(123)

selected <- sample(colnames(protein_raw_numeric), 20)

par(mfrow = c(2,3))

for(prot in selected){
  qqnorm(protein_raw_numeric[[prot]],
         main = prot)
  qqline(protein_raw_numeric[[prot]],
         col = "red")
}
```
---
STAP E: Biologische clustering -> PCA
--- 
```{r}
# PCA-input maken (eiwitten zonder missende waarden)
protein_pca_input <- protein_clean %>%
  select(sample_kit_id, where(~ sum(is.na(.)) == 0))

# PCA uitvoeren met standaardisatie
pca_resultaat <- prcomp(
  protein_pca_input %>% select(-sample_kit_id),
  scale. = TRUE
)

# PC1 en PC2 coordinaten koppelen aan metadata
pca_dataframe <- as.data.frame(pca_resultaat$x[, 1:2]) %>%
  bind_cols(sample_kit_id = protein_pca_input$sample_kit_id) %>%
  inner_join(data_clean, by = "sample_kit_id")

# PCA op leeftijdsgroep
ggplot(pca_dataframe,
       aes(x = PC1,
           y = PC2,
           color = subject.ageGroup)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "PCA van Olink eiwitexpressie",
    subtitle = "Kleuring volgens leeftijdsgroep"
  )

# PCA op CMV-status
ggplot(pca_dataframe,
       aes(x = PC1,
           y = PC2,
           color = cmv_status)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "PCA van Olink eiwitexpressie",
    subtitle = "Kleuring volgens CMV-status"
  )

# PCA op plate ID
ggplot(pca_dataframe,
       aes(x = PC1,
           y = PC2,
           color = as.factor(olink_plate_id))) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "PCA van Olink eiwitexpressie",
    subtitle = "Controle op mogelijke batch-effecten"
  )
```
